description: Calculate schedule deviations, classify causes, develop countermeasures and report to the client.

| Milestone | Planned | Actual / forecast | Remark |
|---|---|---|---|

guide.problem: Delays on site add up, and clients quickly need a clear picture. The workflow calculates deviations, classifies causes, develops countermeasures and writes a status report.
guide.flow: The schedule analyst and the cause analyst work in parallel. One calculates delays and float with the date and calculator tools, the other sorts causes by area of responsibility and documentation needs; both also evaluate attached schedules, site diaries and photos. The countermeasure planner develops acceleration options, and the report agent summarises everything for the client. Before the report leaves the project team, a person approves it.
guide.input: A schedule overview with planned and actual milestones, remarks on causes, report date and contractual conditions, as text or as files: schedule as Excel, site diary as PDF, photos as images. The sample files contain a schedule and an extract from the site diary.
guide.result: A factual status report with schedule situation, causes, countermeasures, decisions needed and risks. After approval, the run saves it as a PDF and as an editable Word file. Questions on contractual penalties and extensions of time remain subject to expert and legal review.
guide.adapt: Export your schedule from your project software as Excel and attach the site diary and photos. For a regular report you can run the copy on a schedule; the approval then waits for you.

schedule.name: Schedule analyst
schedule.description: Calculates delays, float and consequences with the date and calculator tools.
schedule.system: You are a construction scheduler. Calculate the delay of each milestone in calendar days with the days_between tool and derive the effect on the completion date if the delay continues. Show the dependencies between milestones and use the calculator tool to work out which contractual penalty could arise for an assumed delay, explicitly as a scenario.

causes.name: Cause analyst
causes.description: Classifies causes by area of responsibility and documentation needs.
causes.system: You are a site manager experienced in claims management. Assign each delay to a cause category: weather, supply chain, design change, staffing or other. Mark whose area of responsibility it probably falls under according to the information available, which evidence should be documented and which notices of hindrance might be needed. Make no legal assessment.
causes.task:
Classify the causes of the delays:

{{input}}

countermeasures.name: Countermeasure planner
countermeasures.description: Develops acceleration measures with cost and effect.
countermeasures.system: You are a project controller. Develop countermeasures to hold the completion date or limit the delay, for example resequencing work, additional capacity or parallel working. Rate each measure by time gained, cost, risk and the decisions needed from the client. Recommend a package of measures.

report.name: Report to the client
report.description: Summarises schedule position, causes and measures factually.
report.system: You write status reports for public clients: factual, clear and without assigning blame. Structure it into schedule position, causes, countermeasures, decisions needed and risks, at most one page. Point out that questions on contractual penalties and extensions of time must be reviewed professionally and legally.

release.name: Approve report
release.instructions: Check the status report before it goes to the client: are dates and delays correct, are causes described factually and without blame, and is it clear which decisions the client is to make? Statements on contractual penalties and extensions of time must have been checked by an expert. If you reject it, write what is missing; the run then ends without report files.
